### CVE-2021-21408 — Access to restricted PHP code by dynamic static class access in smarty
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2022-01-10 | Updated: 2025-04-23 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-20 CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Smarty is a template engine for PHP, facilitating the separation of presentation (HTML/CSS) from application logic. Prior to versions 3.1.43 and 4.0.3, template authors could run restricted static php methods. Users should upgrade to version 3.1.43 or 4.0.3 to receive a patch.

Affected:
- smarty-php / smarty: affected < 3.1.43; affected >= 4.0.0, < 4.0.3

### CVE-2021-21703 — PHP-FPM memory access in root process leading to privilege escalation
- Assigner: php | Published: 2021-10-25 | Updated: 2024-09-17 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-787 CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write; CWE-284 CWE-284 Improper Access Control
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`

In PHP versions 7.3.x up to and including 7.3.31, 7.4.x below 7.4.25 and 8.0.x below 8.0.12, when running PHP FPM SAPI with main FPM daemon process running as root and child worker processes running as lower-privileged users, it is possible for the child processes to access memory shared with the main process and write to it, modifying it in a way that would cause the root process to conduct invalid memory reads and writes, which can be used to escalate privileges from local unprivileged user to the root user.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 7.3.x <=7.3.31 (custom); affected 7.4.x <7.4.25 (custom); affected 8.0.X <8.0.12 (custom)

Credits: Reported by Charles Fol

### CVE-2021-21708 — UAF due to php_filter_float() failing
- Assigner: php | Published: 2022-02-27 | Updated: 2024-09-17 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:L`

In PHP versions 7.4.x below 7.4.28, 8.0.x below 8.0.16, and 8.1.x below 8.1.3, when using filter functions with FILTER_VALIDATE_FLOAT filter and min/max limits, if the filter fails, there is a possibility to trigger use of allocated memory after free, which can result it crashes, and potentially in overwrite of other memory chunks and RCE. This issue affects: code that uses FILTER_VALIDATE_FLOAT with min/max limits.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 7.4.x <7.4.28 (custom); affected 8.0.X <8.0.16 (custom); affected 8.1.X <8.1.3 (custom)

Credits: dukk at softdev dot online

References:
- https://bugs.php.net/bug.php?id=81708 [x_refsource_MISC]
- https://security.netapp.com/advisory/ntap-20220325-0004/ [x_refsource_CONFIRM]
- https://security.gentoo.org/glsa/202209-20 [vendor-advisory,x_refsource_GENTOO]

### CVE-2021-29454 — Sandbox Escape by math function in smarty
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2022-01-10 | Updated: 2025-04-23 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-74 CWE-74: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Smarty is a template engine for PHP, facilitating the separation of presentation (HTML/CSS) from application logic. Prior to versions 3.1.42 and 4.0.2, template authors could run arbitrary PHP code by crafting a malicious math string. If a math string was passed through as user provided data to the math function, external users could run arbitrary PHP code by crafting a malicious math string. Users should upgrade to version 3.1.42 or 4.0.2 to receive a patch.

Affected:
- smarty-php / smarty: affected < 3.1.42; affected >= 4.0.0, < 4.0.2
